problems.name: No way to evaluate memory or context quality
problems.who: Teams shipping memory-backed or retrieval-backed agents; platform/infra leads who must pick a memory vendor
evidence: "memory is one of the most common sources of subtle, hard-to-reproduce failures"; RAG metrics "don't fully apply" — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/5235

Full-context baseline ~73% beats Mem0 Graph ~68% on LoCoMo; conversations only 16k–26k tokens; no test of knowledge updates — https://blog.getzep.com/lies-damn-lies-statistics-is-mem0-really-sota-in-agent-memory/
Filesystem + grep agent on gpt-4o-mini scored 74.0% on LoCoMo, above Mem0 — https://github.com/lhl/agentic-memory/tree/main/benchmarks
Mem0 self-reports LoCoMo 92.5% and LongMemEval 94.4% in its own 2026 post — https://mem0.ai/blog/ai-memory-benchmarks-in-2026
current_solutions: Generic RAG eval tools (context relevance, answer correctness)
Research benchmarks (BEAM, LoCoMo-Plus, AMA-Bench) not productised
problems.why_unsolved: Memory vendors grade themselves and dispute each other's numbers; public benchmarks are short and recall-only, so full-context beats them; staleness, update propagation and conflict resolution have no standard metrics and no neutral party measuring them.

problems.name: Silent retrieval failures in production RAG
problems.who: Every RAG team; legal, customer-support and finance deployments first
evidence: "The system answers confidently. No error signal is returned." Bad answers discovered weeks or months later — https://www.digitalocean.com/community/conceptual-articles/why-rag-systems-fail-in-production
Naive RAG fails to retrieve the correct context ~40% of the time; a ~50 ms rerank step lifts answer quality 10–25% — https://mudassirkhan.me/blog/production-rag-guide-2026
Stanford Law 2025: legal RAG tools hallucinated 17–33% on 200 queries (as summarised by DigitalOcean) — https://www.digitalocean.com/community/conceptual-articles/why-rag-systems-fail-in-production
current_solutions: Managed RAG (OpenAI file search, Vertex RAG Engine, Bedrock Knowledge Bases)
problems.why_unsolved: Retrieval itself is crowded and increasingly managed by clouds, but detecting a wrong-but-confident answer at serving time is not; no error signal exists, so failures are found by users rather than by the system.

problems.name: Memory write-path junk and hallucination loops
problems.who: Operators of persistent assistants and long-running agents; anyone paying per memory record
evidence: 10,134 entries audited over 32 days, 97.8% junk; only 38 usable as-is — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/4573
808 entries asserting "User prefers Vim" from one hallucination re-extracted in a loop; "a better model ... extracts more indiscriminately" — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/4573
130 security/privacy leak entries and 315 hallucinated user profiles found in the same store — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/4573
Concurrent add() calls both pass dedup and write identical memories (TOCTOU) — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/6531
current_solutions: Cloud extraction with bundled consolidation (Google Memory Bank, AgentCore built-in strategy at $0.75/1,000 records)
problems.why_unsolved: Extraction is a prompt, not a gate: recalled memories re-enter extraction context and get re-stored, stronger models follow the permissive prompt more faithfully, and metered vendors are paid per record so have no incentive to reject entries.

problems.name: Policy constraints dropped by compaction
problems.who: Enterprises running long-horizon agents with tool access; security and compliance owners
evidence: ConstraintRot: 1,323 episodes, 7 model families; violations 0% with full policy context, 30% after compaction, up to 59% for some models — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22528
Constraint dropped by summary → 38% violation rate; survived → 0%; Constraint Pinning restores 0% — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22528
CLAUDE.md standing instructions drop out after /compact; users request automatic re-injection — https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/24460
current_solutions: Re-injecting system prompt after compaction by hand
Guardrail models at the tool-call boundary
problems.why_unsolved: Vendors ship lossy summarisation with no fidelity guarantee; constraint pinning exists only as a paper; enterprises run multiple model vendors, so a policy layer that survives every vendor's compaction is not something any single vendor will build.

problems.name: Memory poisoning and privacy leakage
problems.who: Security teams; multi-tenant agent platforms where untrusted users can write to memory
evidence: MINJA achieves over 95% injection success with query-only access; poisoned memory survives resets and model updates — https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03704
"robust Long-Term Memory security cannot be retrofitted at retrieval or execution time alone" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.16548
Open-source router tracks memory-injection defence as a backlog item — https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/1386
Mem0 audit found 130 security/privacy leak entries in one production store — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/4573
current_solutions: Academic defences (MEMSAD, SMSR, MemAudit) not productised
Generic prompt-injection filters at input time
problems.why_unsolved: Attacks are persistent, stateful and propagate across sessions, so retrieval-time filtering is insufficient; storage-time provenance, versioning and policy-aware retention do not exist in shipped memory layers; incidents lag papers, so buyers are not yet forced to act.

problems.name: Cost and cache opacity at 100:1 input ratios
problems.who: Platform teams running agents at scale; FinOps and engineering managers
evidence: ~100:1 input:output token ratio, ~50 tool calls per task; cached Sonnet $0.30/MTok vs $3 uncached; "a single-token difference can invalidate the cache" — https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus
Compaction pass billed as a separate iteration; top-level usage excludes it — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction

Azure customers cannot see how many input tokens server-side state contributes per turn under previous_response_id — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5791830/azure-openai-response-api-input-token-counting-wit
Runtime duration and long-term memory dominate AgentCore bills (June 2026) — https://www.cipherprojects.com/blog/posts/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-pricing-2026/
current_solutions: Vendor usage dashboards and cache-hit metrics
Manual prompt-prefix discipline and tool masking
problems.why_unsolved: Each vendor exposes its own partial accounting; server-side state and compaction move cost out of the request the developer sees; cross-vendor attribution of context cost to features or tenants is nobody's native job.

problems.name: Retention, deletion and provenance of agent memory
problems.who: Regulated enterprises (finance, health, EU data subjects); privacy and legal teams
evidence: 435-work survey: literature "concentrates more heavily on accumulating and retrieving state than on governing, recovering, or relinquishing it" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30306
Unlearned data re-enters via the other pathway (parameters vs external memory); deletion must be synchronised — https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17692
AgentCore short-term events cannot expire below 7 days; 30/90-day retention cannot be force-expired — https://cloudburn.io/blog/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-pricing
Mem0 has no built-in expiration or decay (#5330, cited in #6531) — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/6531
current_solutions: Cloud retention settings with fixed minimums
problems.why_unsolved: Memory systems are built to accumulate; provenance, versioning and rollback are absent in shipped layers; cloud minimum-retention rules conflict with deletion obligations; backflow between parameters and stores makes deletion hard to prove.

problems.name: Mid-task compaction loses work state
problems.who: Coding-agent users (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline); builders of agent harnesses
evidence: "Auto-compact triggers ... no user control, no warning before compaction"; summary "loses track of file modifications, intermediate decisions, specific technical details" — https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/10948
Skills context "completely lost after auto-compaction, causing repeated errors and massive productivity loss" — https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/13919
Cline compacts under 200K on a 1M model and "gets a little lost"; redoes completed tasks — https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/9181
"Summarization is inherently lossy and the blocking call stalls agent inference for tens of seconds" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23296
current_solutions: Anthropic server-side compaction (150k default trigger, custom instructions, pause_after_compaction)
Research: ARC addressable recall, parallel compaction, CompactionRL
problems.why_unsolved: Summarisation is lossy by construction and the harness vendors own the trigger; but both Anthropic and OpenAI shipped server-side compaction in early 2026 and are iterating, so a third party cannot out-ship them on the mechanism itself.

problems.name: Multi-agent handoff loses decisions
problems.who: Teams building subagent or orchestrator systems
evidence: Subagents without shared traces make conflicting implicit decisions (Flappy Bird example); share full traces not messages — https://cognition.com/blog/dont-build-multi-agents
"The most pressing open challenge is multi-agent memory consistency" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10062
LangChain: the failure is context sharing, not parallelism — https://www.langchain.com/blog/how-and-when-to-build-multi-agent-systems
current_solutions: Framework-level state sharing (LangGraph, Agents SDK handoffs)
Shared memory layers (Mem0, Redis, Neo4j via Microsoft Agent Framework)
problems.why_unsolved: Consistency semantics for shared agent memory are undefined; frameworks pass messages, not decisions; the problem is real but the buyer population running production multi-agent systems is still small.

problems.name: Stale and contradictory memories outrank fresh ones
problems.who: Personal-assistant, CRM and support agents tracking mutable user attributes
evidence: ADD-only extraction accumulates contradictions; retrieval returns outdated info as top candidate because scoring lacks recency — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/4956
Proposed metrics include staleness score and update-propagation rate — https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/5235
Google Memory Bank "consolidates new memories with existing ones and resolves contradictions" — https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/vertex-ai-memory-bank-in-public-preview
current_solutions: OpenAI Agents SDK consolidation agent with recency-based forgetting
problems.why_unsolved: Open-source layers still use ADD-only pipelines without recency weighting, but cloud vendors already ship consolidation and contradiction resolution, so the residual gap is narrowing fast.

problems.name: Coding-agent session reset; static instruction files
problems.who: Developers on Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Windsurf
evidence: copilot-instructions.md is "static text" with "no concept of time"; "Every AI coding assistant on the market has the same constraint" — https://memnexus.ai/blog/2026-02-20-github-copilot-persistent-memory
Windsurf Memories persist context across conversations; Cascade tracks edits, commands and terminal output — https://codeant.ai/blogs/best-ai-code-editor-cursor-vs-windsurf-vs-copilot
OpenAI Agents SDK sandbox memory distils lessons into MEMORY.md across runs — https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox/memory/
problems.why_unsolved: It is largely solved: every IDE and SDK vendor bundles persistent memory; what remains is quality, which is the eval and hygiene problem above, not a session-memory product.

problems.name: Context rot: effective window below advertised
problems.who: Everyone using long inputs; long-session agent users
evidence: 18 models tested; focused input ~300 tokens vs full ~113k; all models degrade, Claude Opus 4 largest gap — https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot
"Claude Code with Opus or Sonnet gets worse the more compactions happen, quality regresses" — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44564248
"Even LLMs with 1M token context windows (with and without retrieval-augmentation) struggle as dialogues lengthen" — https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27246
current_solutions: Keep context small: compaction, context editing, retrieval
Redis, Letta and others positioning memory layers as the fix

problems.name: Tool-schema and tool-result bloat
problems.who: MCP users; teams on local or cheap models
evidence: A 106-tool MCP server injects 54,600 tokens at every initialisation; lazy hydration cuts it to 4,899 — https://layered.dev/mcp-tool-schema-bloat-the-hidden-token-tax-and-how-to-fix-it/
Anthropic example: 150,000 tokens → 2,000 tokens (98.7% reduction) with code execution — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp
Tool descriptions can mean "hundreds of thousands of tokens before reading a request"; transcript flows through twice — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45954572
current_solutions: Anthropic Tool Search Tool and context editing (clear_tool_uses)
Code execution with MCP / Cloudflare Code Mode
problems.why_unsolved: It is being solved natively: Anthropic, Cloudflare and the MCP spec process all shipped on-demand tool loading between Nov 2025 and early 2026; developers fix the rest with configuration and do not pay for it.

problems.name: Hosted-memory lock-in; no portability or integrity proof
problems.who: Buyers of hosted memory services; platform teams fearing vendor dependence
evidence: Mem0 cloud memory: "no cryptographic verification of memory integrity", no portability to other systems — https://baheet.medium.com/whoever-owns-the-memory-owns-the-agent-b2fc5b726457
Portable Agent Memory protocol proposes provenance-verified cross-vendor transfer — https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11032v1
Microsoft Agent Framework makes memory backends pluggable (Foundry, Mem0, Redis, Neo4j) — https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/microsoft-agent-framework-version-1-0/
current_solutions: Self-hosted OSS memory (Cognee, Mem0 OSS, Letta)
problems.why_unsolved: Vendors have no incentive to make memory portable and no evidence shows buyers paying for portability; it is a talking point, not a budget line, so it stays a feature of open-source layers rather than a product.

wedges.name: Neutral memory and context quality CI
wedges.icp: Teams shipping memory-backed or retrieval-backed agents; platform leads choosing between Mem0, Zep, Cognee, Letta, Memory Bank and AgentCore
wedges.why_now: Benchmark wars: Zep shows a full-context baseline (~73%) beating Mem0 (~68%) on 16k–26k-token LoCoMo while Mem0 self-reports 92.5%; mem0 #5235 (May 2026) asks for staleness, conflict-resolution and update-propagation metrics; Memory Bank and AgentCore began billing per record in Feb 2026, so buyers now pay for something nobody measures
wedges.moat: A labelled corpus of real memory and compaction failures from replayed production traces; position as the referee every vendor submits to and none can be; CI integration creates switching cost

wedges.name: Store-agnostic memory write-gate
wedges.icp: Operators of persistent assistants and long-running agents paying per memory record on Mem0, Zep, Memory Bank or AgentCore
wedges.why_now: mem0 #4573 (Mar 2026) audited 10,134 entries and found 97.8% junk, 808 copies of one hallucination, 130 leaks; AgentCore charges $0.75 per 1,000 records and metered vendors have no incentive to reject; stronger models extract more indiscriminately
wedges.moat: Gate rules learned from the failure corpus produced by the eval wedge; sits at the one control point every store shares (the write path); provenance stamps become the audit trail enterprises later pay for
examples: Mnemora and Mnemosyne (no-LLM write path entrants)

wedges.name: Cross-vendor policy pinning sidecar
wedges.icp: Security and compliance owners at enterprises running long-horizon, tool-using agents across more than one model vendor
wedges.why_now: ConstraintRot (Jun 2026): violations 0% with full policy, 30% after compaction, 59% for some models, 0% with pinning; claude-code #24460 requesting CLAUDE.md re-injection was closed as not planned (Feb 2026); Anthropic and OpenAI now expose compaction instructions and pause_after_compaction as API parameters, so the hooks exist but the product does not
wedges.moat: Policy library plus violation audit trail across vendors; compliance certifications (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAA, BYOC) in the Zep pattern; a single model vendor will not build a layer that survives every other vendor's compaction
examples: Guardrail models at the tool-call boundary

wedges.name: Serving-time retrieval failure detection
wedges.icp: Legal, customer-support and finance RAG teams where a confident wrong answer is costly
wedges.why_now: No error signal exists at serving time; legal RAG tools hallucinated 17–33% in Stanford's 2025 study; managed RAG (OpenAI file search, Vertex RAG Engine, Bedrock Knowledge Bases) absorbed retrieval but not detection
wedges.moat: Vertical-specific labelled failure data and abstain thresholds; low otherwise, since groundedness scoring is a feature cloud guardrails can add

wedges.name: Compliance-grade memory for regulated buyers
wedges.icp: Finance, health and EU data controllers whose privacy and legal teams must prove retention, deletion and provenance of agent memory
wedges.why_now: AgentCore cannot expire short-term events under 7 days and 30/90-day retention cannot be force-expired; a 435-work survey finds the field ignores governing and relinquishing state; no shipped layer has versioning or rollback
wedges.moat: Certifications, audit logs and BYOC that better-funded rivals gate behind sales; Zep's eight-person team shows it is ownable but you would be a follower
examples: Zep (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAA, BYOC, EU DPA)

wedges.name: Cross-vendor context cost attribution
wedges.icp: Platform and FinOps teams running agents at scale across Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure and Bedrock
wedges.why_now: Manus reports ~100:1 input:output over ~50 tool calls with a 10x cached/uncached price gap; Anthropic bills compaction as a separate iteration summed in usage.iterations; Azure cannot show tokens contributed by previous_response_id state
wedges.moat: Low: gateways and observability vendors already hold the request path and will add cache and compaction accounting

wedges.name: Shared decision ledger for multi-agent systems
wedges.icp: Teams running orchestrator and subagent systems in production
wedges.why_now: Surveys name multi-agent memory consistency the most pressing open challenge (2026); Cognition and LangChain both locate the failure in context sharing, yet frameworks still pass messages rather than decisions
wedges.moat: Consistency semantics nobody has defined; but the production buyer population is still small and frameworks can bundle shared state
